R	2023	02054TRSCB66MAI	TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	NORFOLK	MA	02054			TRESCA BROTHERS SAND & GRAVEL	66 MAIN ST	MILLIS	MA		02054	YES	NO	NO	NO	NO	NO	THOMAS TRESCA	5083268827		THOMAS@TRESCACONCRETE.COM								327320	327331					42.1782	-71.3245	005784152		MAD005784152										MAR05CT82	MAR053048											NA				110003423180	1323222014235	N511	N511	Nitrate compounds (water dissociable; reportable only when in aqueous solution)	NA	NO	TRI	NO	NO	NO	NO			829450	8.11	B4	B4 - Source reduction activities were implemented but were unsuccessful.	Tresca has been conducting toxics use reduction planning with a MassDEP certified toxics use reduction planner, but there are barriers to source reduction.  Nitrate compounds are contained in some of the admixtures used by Tresca.  These admixtures are used because they conform to the most stringent chloride ion limits required by concrete industry standards.  Chloride ion constraints are typically in place for concrete used in coastal environments.  Other issued with using chloride ions include corrosion to reinforced steel, drying shrinkage, creep, heat evolution, and resistance to sulfate attack.  In addition, there is potential energy savings with using these admixtures by reducing curing temperatures and/or steaming time.  No nitrate compound waste is generated since the raw material is completely incorporated into the final product.  The admixture is delivered and stored in bulk and is automatically dispensed, so no residue is generated.  Tresca has considered many other alternative admixtures, but they have an increase in health or physical hazards, would use more nitrate compounds, have increased mixing times, decrease the strength of the concrete, have a shorter shelf life, and/or are not economically feasible.	Barriers to P2

The gas addressed by the FGTU is material that has been traditionally sent to flare as necessary without further sulfur-recovery treatment. In the event of malfunction or non-availability of this unit, such gases would still go directly to flare. The additional equipment and operation is aimed at reducing intermittent flare emissions of sulfur dioxide, particularly during certain periods of startup/shutdown and malfunction. Sulfur material captured during such periods is stored on-site as amine salts for subsequent treatment and resource recovery in the existing fuel gas treatment facility (MSCC's amine unit) and MSCC's sulfur recovery plant during normal operation of those portions of the facility. The FGTU uses an amine treatment contactor to remove H2S from selected gases during these situations prior to flaring, along with liquid storage. R	2023	7044WLNCXX11437	LEI INC.	11437 FONTANA LN	AMITE	TANGIPAHOA PARISH	LA	70443			LEI INC.	P.O. BOX 550	INDEPENDENCE	LA		70443	YES	NO	NO	NO	NO	NO	LANDYN OLLER	9858788210	400	LOLLER@LEIRECYCLE.COM								562211						30.645202	-90.532796	849359997																						MAX ENVIRONMENTAL HOLDINGS INC		MAX ENVIRONMENTAL HOLDINGS INC				110071174324	1323221558721	7439-97-6	0007439976	Mercury	NA	NO	PBT	YES	NO	NO	YES			778849	8.11	RECY	Recycling	Please find listed below, and attached, the description of the MP8000 Lamp Recycling Plant and the engineering controls utilized for controlling air emissions; The plant comprises of: - One Crusher with Main Hopper and Separation Unit for whole fluorescent tubes. The crushed debris is conveyed evenly to the Main Separator. This causes agitation of the debris and allows the resultant mercury bearing phosphor powder to be drawn off by two Air Extraction Filter Units. The debris discharges from the end of the Separation Unit over a Magnet that separates the glass from the metal components, which are conveyed to suitable collection bins. This Separator processes fluorescent tubes and all other types of lamp glass with magnetic metal components in one operation. One Secondary Separator to accept all types of both whole and crushed lamps. This unit separates the glass from the other components and acts as a “primary cleaner” for drums of indeterminate debris. The glass cullet is conveyed back to the Main Hopper for feeding and cleaning through the Main Separator whilst the mix of other materials is discharged into a collection bin at the end. The merit of this unit is that when lamps of one type are loaded it will discharge one type of debris such as plastic from modern low energy CFL lamps. If however a mixture of lamps is loaded then a mixture of components will be discharged. None of these components are suitable for further treatment through the Recycling Plant. Two fan assisted Filter Units are used to draw off all mercury bearing phosphor powder and vapor from the contents of the lamps down to 5 micron size. These ensure the plant operates at negative pressure. Each unit extracts approximately 2800m3 per hour and uses 6 filters which are polyester pleated with PTFE coating. All finer dusts and vapors that pass through the filters are ducted to our Main Filter Stack containing approximately 2 cubic meters of Sulphur based Activated Carbon, with which the mercury reacts and allows the exhausted air to be mercury free and ducted to atmosphere. The waste stream from the plant first enters a Flow equalization Tank where all the waste product, equipment and tank washes, rinses, and floor drains are contained and further diluted with washdown water.
